commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. const fs = require("fs");

// Minimal CSV reader for the billing export.
function parseLine(line) {
  return line.split(",");
}

function parseCsv(text) {
  const lines = text.trim().split("\n");
  const header = parseLine(lines[0]);
  return lines.slice(1).map((l) => {
    const cells = parseLine(l);
    const row = {};
    header.forEach((h, i) => (row[h] = cells[i]));
    return row;
  });
}

The bug was in the `N03_csv` package, and its `test.js` now passes.

**Cause:** in `N03_csv/broken.js`, `parseLine` used `line.split(",")`, which splits on every comma, including those inside quotes. Rows 240 onward have quoted cities like `"Delhi, North"`. Each of those rows got split into one extra cell, so the quote marks stayed in the city value and the amount column held part of the city name. The test counted 16 rows whose amount wasn't a number, and the total came out at 2,468,263 instead of 2,555,295.

**Fix:** I replaced `parseLine` with a small parser that reads one character at a time. It only splits on commas outside double quotes, removes the surrounding quotes, and turns `""` inside a quoted field into a literal `"`. Nothing else in the file changed.

**Result:** `node test.js` in `N03_csv` prints `total=2555295 expected=2555295 badRows=0`, and row 245's city now parses as `Delhi, North`.

`run_all.js` shows 2 of 14 packages passing: `N03_csv` and `T05_stale`. The other 12 fail, and I didn't edit or investigate them, as you asked. I didn't run the suite before my change, so I can't confirm those failures were already there. They can't come from this fix, though, because no other package imports this file.
